a39.speaker: Charles Masubi, GGML Senior Human Resources Manager
a39.name: Charles Masubi
a39.title: GGML Senior Human Resources Manager
a39.speech: "Our goal is to contribute to the development of Tanzania's workforce by giving young graduates the opportunity to gain real work experience and industry-standard professional skills. We are proud to see our graduates succeed within GGML and in other institutions. This is something with long-term benefits for individuals and for the development of the region as a whole."

a39.speaker: National Bureau of Statistics (Tanzania)
a39.name: National Bureau of Statistics (Tanzania)
a39.speech: Cited as the source showing unemployment among youth aged 16 to 34 remains a major challenge, with thousands of graduates entering the job market every year without the work experience employers require.

a104.speaker: Residents living next to the national parks
a104.name: Residents living next to the national parks
a104.speech: Have recently complained of being encroached upon by the animals for which they made way in the reserves, saying elephants endanger villagers' lives and destroy farms, creating the danger of famine, and that pupils in those areas cannot go to school for fear for their safety.

a104.speaker: Wildlife conservation authorities
a104.name: Wildlife conservation authorities
a104.speech: Direct the blame at the farmers, claiming that they are invading the reserve areas.

a104.speaker: The author's Geography teacher
a104.name: The author's Geography teacher
a104.speech: Told me that when one animal is eaten it creates a continuation of new life for them; whenever they are attacked they scatter to start new families or mix with other communities and produce new offspring.

a244.speaker: Ukrainian Foreign Ministry (statement)
a244.name: Ukrainian Foreign Ministry (statement)
a244.speech: According to a statement issued by the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry, Ginkel was "invited" to a discussion by Foreign Minister Andrey Sybiga on Wednesday; during the talks the Ukrainians emphasized "the critical importance of continuing the deliveries of previously allocated defense packages," particularly air defense systems, and the US envoy was informed that any "delay or procrastination in supporting Ukraine's defense capabilities" would prolong the conflict.

a244.speaker: The New York Times, Politico and NBC News (media reports)
a244.name: The New York Times
a244.title: Politico and NBC News (media reports)
a244.speech: Reported that the US has paused shipments of Patriot missile interceptors, GMLRS rockets, Hellfire missiles, and thousands of 155mm artillery shells; NBC reported that some of these shipments had already arrived in Europe but were withheld from being transferred to Ukrainian forces.

a244.speaker: Ukraine's Defense Ministry (statement)
a244.name: Ukraine's Defense Ministry (statement)
a244.speech: Has not confirmed the pause in weapon deliveries from the US; in a statement on Wednesday, it said that it is "clarifying the current factual circumstances of the supplies," stressing that Kiev has not received any official notifications about the suspension.

a244.speaker: Media reports (on the Pentagon)
a244.name: Media reports (on the Pentagon)
a244.speech: According to media reports, the Pentagon halted the deliveries after US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered a review of available weapons stockpiles, citing concerns over munitions depletion.

a244.speaker: Anna Kelly, White House Deputy Press Secretary
a244.name: Anna Kelly
a244.title: White House Deputy Press Secretary
a244.speech: Has confirmed that some transfers had been paused following a Department of Defense assessment of global commitments, stating that "this decision was made to put America's interests first."

a244.speaker: Military experts and senior Western officials, including Vladimir Zelensky
a244.name: Military experts and senior Western officials
a244.title: including Vladimir Zelensky
a244.speech: Have repeatedly acknowledged that without foreign munitions, Ukraine would lose the conflict in fairly short order.

a244.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a244.name: Donald Trump
a244.title: US President
a244.speech: Said the Patriot air defense systems were "very hard to get" and that the US needed them for its own defense and for Israel.

a244.speaker: Russia
a244.name: Russia
a244.speech: Has consistently condemned Western arm shipments to Ukraine, arguing that they only serve to prolong hostilities and lead to more bloodshed without affecting the inevitable outcome of the conflict.

a268.speaker: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) data
a268.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) data
a268.speech: According to OECD data, sub-Saharan Africa absorbed nearly 40% of USAID's annual budget.

a268.speaker: The White House
a268.name: The White House
a268.speech: According to the White House, USAID's missions will from now on be integrated directly into a Directorate-General for Cooperation and Development attached to the US State Department; officially the aim is to streamline the structure, limit administrative duplication and strengthen the alignment between development aid and the diplomatic priorities of the United States.

a268.speaker: World Bank
a268.name: World Bank
a268.speech: recalls that the agency was among the top five bilateral donors for the Sustainable Development Goals relating to health, education and gender equality.

a268.speaker: Government Accountability Office (GAO) report
a268.name: Government Accountability Office (GAO) report
a268.speech: underlines that USAID managed more than 1,300 projects in 80 overseas missions, sometimes with duplication between federal agencies.

a268.speaker: US administration
a268.name: US administration
a268.speech: presents the dissolution as a measure of sound management of public funds and defends a refocusing on major diplomatic priorities, in a context of increased rivalry with China over investments in Africa and Asia.

a268.speaker: Several US officials
a268.name: Several US officials
a268.speech: find that USAID's strength lay precisely in its operational autonomy and its technical expertise; according to them, the technical expertise accumulated over decades by USAID's teams could be diluted, or even lost, within a broader diplomatic apparatus in which aid risks becoming a mere instrument of geopolitical influence.

a268.speaker: Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa
a268.name: Claver Gatete
a268.title: Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa
a268.speech: "Aid can no longer be regarded as a reliable or sustainable solution. Time is short. We must act now, with you, our heads of state, who are leading reforms, creating an enabling environment and mobilising domestic resources. Together, we can fulfil the promise of Agenda 2063 and the SDGs," he stated recently at the eleventh session of the Africa Regional Forum on Sustainable Development held in Kampala, Uganda.

a268.speaker: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, statistician-economist, specialist in economic policy management
a268.name: Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi
a268.title: statistician-economist, specialist in economic policy management
a268.speech: "Efforts must be made to diversify sources of financing by turning to regional and international financial markets and to innovative financing. The most predictable and most sustainable resources are domestic public resources."

a382.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a382.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a382.title: President of Zanzibar
a382.speech: Directed Regional Commissioners to strictly enforce land laws and plan guidelines to curb unauthorised construction; said that only landowners with valid titles and permits will be eligible for government compensation, particularly in areas needed for development projects. “The government cannot continue to pay large sums to people who build illegally in reserved areas, without any official documents. This trend must stop.” ; Pointed out that many government farms and land reserves have already been illegally occupied and developed, leading to a shortage of available land, giving examples of rubber plantations and other state-owned lands that have been invaded, and cautioning that such individuals should not expect compensation: “Let it be clear, if someone builds in a government area without permission, they will not be compensated.” ; Urged local authorities, from Shehas and district officers to Regional Commissioners, to ensure that no construction is allowed without the proper permits: “As you travel from Urban to North or South Unguja, you see unplanned construction everywhere, even on clearly designated government lands. This must stop.”

a382.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a382.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a382.title: President of Zanzibar
a382.speech: Reiterated the government's commitment to modern, well-planned cities with proper infrastructure including roads, water and electricity; announced that the government will continue investing in affordable housing and tasked relevant institutions to fulfil their responsibilities in land management; commended the Ministry of Lands and Housing for its innovation in establishing the Land and Housing Week, encouraging that the event be held annually; stressed that land is a limited and valuable resource that must be protected for national development, including sectors such as tourism, agriculture, industry and public services; praised the Ministry's efforts to develop the new Property Valuation Guideline, which aims to ensure transparency, fairness and consistency in compensation for land acquired for development projects.

a382.speaker: Rahma Kassim Ali, Minister for Lands and Housing
a382.name: Rahma Kassim Ali
a382.title: Minister for Lands and Housing
a382.speech: Urged citizens to treat land as a shared national resource that must be preserved through joint efforts; expressed gratitude to President Mwinyi for his leadership, which she said has significantly improved the ministry's operations and helped reduce land disputes.

a382.speaker: Mhaza Gharib Juma, Deputy Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Lands and Housing
a382.name: Mhaza Gharib Juma
a382.title: Deputy Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Lands and Housing
a382.speech: Said that over 3,570 land plots have been formally identified, with 303 legal titles issued to citizens; said the newly launched valuation guideline outlines steps, standards and procedures to ensure fair and timely compensation for development projects.

a382.speaker: Ayoub Mohammed Mahmoud, South Unguja Regional Commissioner
a382.name: Ayoub Mohammed Mahmoud
a382.title: South Unguja Regional Commissioner
a382.speech: On behalf of Zanzibar's regional leaders, welcomed the new detailed land-use plans, describing them as essential tools to prevent misuse of land and enforce proper development controls; affirmed the regions' readiness to collaborate with the Ministry to ensure that Zanzibar's land retains its value, appearance, and integrity for future generations.

a412.speaker: Bahraini Foreign Minister
a412.name: Bahraini Foreign Minister
a412.speech: “The ‘Palestine Summit’ embodied Arab unity in support of a just and comprehensive peace based on the two-state solution and the reconstruction of the Gaza Strip.”

a412.speaker: President of the Republic of Lebanon (at the Arab Summit)
a412.name: President of the Republic of Lebanon (at the Arab Summit)
a412.speech: “The Arab dimension of the Palestinian question requires that we all be strong. There is still land occupied by Israel and Lebanese prisoners in its jails. We will not give up our land and we will not abandon our prisoners.”

a538.speaker: Minister of Labour and the Civil Service of Guinea
a538.name: Minister of Labour and the Civil Service of Guinea
a538.speech: Asked the National Gendarmerie to ensure compliance with the measures prohibiting the movement of administrative vehicles without express authorisation outside working hours and working days, as part of the implementation of Order A/2022/3135/MTFP/CAB/SGG.

a538.speaker: High Commander of the National Gendarmerie and Director of Military Justice
a538.name: High Commander of the National Gendarmerie and Director of Military Justice
a538.speech: Underlines the importance of these measures, which aim to ensure the appropriate use of the State's resources and to prevent abuses ; instructed gendarmerie unit commanders to proceed with the systematic immobilisation, carried out courteously, of any vehicle concerned encountered by their patrols and checkpoints, to take it to the nearest gendarmerie unit and to report to the Operations Centre of the High Command.

a725.speaker: U.S. Embassy in South Sudan (press statement)
a725.name: U.S. Embassy in South Sudan (press statement)
a725.speech: In a press statement, paid tribute to the “courageous” South Sudanese girls and young women, some of whom it said are already engaging in initiatives to break barriers that hold them back in society: “Girls and women deserve a prosperous and secure future, free from gender-based violence and discrimination” ; “We call on the transitional government to actively address the challenges faced by girls to fulfill their dreams of becoming changemakers, innovators, entrepreneurs, service members, activists, and responsible citizens” ; “This should be a future marked by peace, human rights, democracy, and a government responsive to its people’s needs.”

a725.speaker: U.S. Embassy in South Sudan (press statement)
a725.name: U.S. Embassy in South Sudan (press statement)
a725.speech: The statement underscored Washington’s continued support to help girls remain in school in South Sudan and acquire skills and knowledge through funding from the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID); the diplomatic mission said this support is provided to empower girls so that they and their families lead healthier, productive and peaceful lives.

a725.speaker: U.S. government
a725.name: U.S. government
a725.speech: Urges the transitional government to initiate policies that help young women achieve their dreams, and said it is committed to helping girls to actively take part in achieving a peaceful future that opens opportunities for them and all South Sudanese people.

a725.speaker: Aid agencies
a725.name: Aid agencies
a725.speech: Girls in South Sudan face enormous challenges including gender inequality, poverty, and early marriage, among others, according to aid agencies.

a725.speaker: UNFPA (UN population agency) survey
a725.name: UNFPA (UN population agency) survey
a725.speech: According to a survey by the UN’s population agency, UNFPA, the country accounts for the second highest prevalence case of Gender Based Violence in the East African region.

a725.speaker: Member of parliament (unnamed)
a725.name: Member of parliament (unnamed)
a725.speech: Disclosed that controversial aspects such as customary marriages and the recognition of marital rape have prolonged deliberations on the Anti-Gender-Based Violence Bill.

a725.speaker: Women activists and women’s rights groups in South Sudan
a725.name: Women activists and women’s rights groups in South Sudan
a725.speech: Have been advocating for the adoption of an Anti-GBV bill that was drafted in 2019 and is widely seen as an opportunity to address violence against women and girls, and various stakeholders and women’s rights groups have persistently urged for its enactment.

a953.speaker: United States government
a953.name: United States government
a953.speech: has called on the Lesotho government to intensify its efforts in combating corruption, bolstering press freedom, and upholding the rule of law.

a953.speaker: Thomas Hines, Chargé d'Affaires at the US Embassy in Maseru
a953.name: Thomas Hines
a953.title: Chargé d'Affaires at the US Embassy in Maseru
a953.speech: stressed the damaging effects of corruption on the economy and society while presenting Lesotho's 2025 Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) scorecard to the government this week; underscored the importance of addressing corruption and strengthening press freedom and rule of law to achieve the Compacts' goals of improving healthcare access, fostering employment and business development, and boosting investment in high-value crop production ; “Regression in control of corruption puts Lesotho at risk of failing in the scorecard” ; expressed the US government's commitment to partnering with Lesotho to tackle these issues.

a953.speaker: Thomas Hines, Chargé d'Affaires at the US Embassy in Maseru
a953.name: Thomas Hines
a953.title: Chargé d'Affaires at the US Embassy in Maseru
a953.speech: highlighted Lesotho's strong overall performance, noting that the country passed 17 out of 20 indicators this year, up from 15 last year ; “Not only did Lesotho pass, but it also improved its performance, reflecting the country's, the Prime Minister's, and his government's commitment to strengthening democratic governance and fostering economic prosperity” ; praised Lesotho's achievements in areas such as girls' primary education completion rates, natural resource protection, land rights and access, and fiscal policy, and lauded the government for passing critical legislation, including inheritance reforms, labour, occupational health and safety laws ; “These reforms not only enhance the impact of the MCC Compact but also underscore the strength of the US-Lesotho partnership, reflecting more than 20 years of cooperation between MCC and Lesotho.”

a953.speaker: 2025 Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) scorecard (report)
a953.name: 2025 Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) scorecard (report)
a953.speech: Lesotho's score on corruption control dropped from 85 percent to 79 percent, raising concerns about the nation's performance in this critical area; Lesotho is among only 26 countries that passed the scorecard, while 50 others failed.

a953.speaker: Nthomeng Majara, Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho, speaking on behalf of Prime Minister Sam Matekane
a953.name: Nthomeng Majara
a953.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho, speaking on behalf of Prime Minister Sam Matekane
a953.speech: acknowledged the need for the government to redouble its efforts in combating corruption and addressing areas of concern identified in the scorecard; reaffirmed the government's unwavering commitment to eliminating corruption ; “We do not have any untouchables. If any of us must go and answer for corruption, they will have to face the law.” ; promised intensified efforts in areas such as trade policy, government effectiveness, and freedom of information ; “We further commit that in the coming year, the government will focus on these policy areas to address deficiencies. The government remains steadfast in its commitment to investing in our people and ensuring equality of opportunities for every Mosotho, regardless of their background or location.”

a953.speaker: Nthomeng Majara, Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho
a953.name: Nthomeng Majara
a953.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho
a953.speech: said the government had succeeded in improving girls' primary education completion rates, attributing the progress to Prime Minister Matekane's commitment to submitting data for assessment ; “This achievement is a testament to our dedication to empowering young girls through education. We are proud of the progress we have made and aim to achieve even more positive results in the coming year.”

a1028.speaker: Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Vice-President of Ghana
a1028.name: Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang
a1028.title: Vice-President of Ghana
a1028.speech: Said the government will work and collaborate with civic stakeholders to build consensus towards the passage of the Non-Profit Bill into law: "There is currently no specific law in place that facilitates the activities of CSOs and nurtures the development of the civil society space" ; said the government would enhance tax incentives to encourage the local philanthropic ecosystem and deepen partnerships with community-led initiatives targeting social and economic challenges ; "We will examine our policies and legislation to ensure easier registration of NGOs, community foundations, and philanthropic organisations."

a1028.speaker: Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Vice-President of Ghana
a1028.name: Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang
a1028.title: Vice-President of Ghana
a1028.speech: Said it was important for the country to work hard towards self-sufficiency and move away from aid dependency to ensure sustainable growth through domestic investment and inclusive financial innovation; said the country, like many in the Global South, was under pressure while the World Bank's official development assistance, historically a cornerstone of development financing, was now declining along with traditional aid flows; said many donor countries were grappling with political shifts, leading to aid cuts or reallocation away from development cooperation ; "External concessional financing is also increasingly limited. Public debt is rising. And the fiscal space for government to respond to basic needs is becoming narrower" ; "All these signals that we cannot rely on aid as the primary engine of development. We are being challenged to think differently and, as a government, create an enabling environment to boost domestic investment and mobilise new forms of financing."

a1028.speaker: Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Vice-President of Ghana
a1028.name: Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang
a1028.title: Vice-President of Ghana
a1028.speech: Said the country and many African nations were reexamining models that rely solely on aid: "We are deepening domestic resource mobilisation, broadening the tax base, and reforming the public financial management system"; said the government was also committed to creating an enabling environment where civic actors would be empowered.

a1028.speaker: Alhaji Ibrahim-Tanko Amidu, Executive Director of STAR-Ghana Foundation and Convener of the forum
a1028.name: Alhaji Ibrahim-Tanko Amidu
a1028.title: Executive Director of STAR-Ghana Foundation and Convener of the forum
a1028.speech: Said that most CSOs in the country relied heavily on funding from bilateral donors and philanthropic foundations, adding that "The shrinking of international aid has serious implications - not just for the financing of civil society activities - but for the very survival of the sector" ; encouraged young people to explore new and unconventional ways of organising civic efforts that break free from outdated models ; "We must rethink what civil society looks like, how it operates, and how it brings stronger, younger, and more diverse voices into national development conversations."

a1028.speaker: Osama Makawi, United Nations Resident Coordinator in Ghana (speech read on her behalf by UNESCO Country Representative Edmond Moukala)
a1028.name: Osama Makawi
a1028.title: United Nations Resident Coordinator in Ghana (speech read on her behalf by UNESCO Country Representative Edmond Moukala)
a1028.speech: Reaffirmed the UN's commitment to support the country's national development priorities through strengthened partnerships, innovative financing mechanisms and inclusive policy dialogue.

a1059.speaker: Osman Saleh, Foreign Minister of Eritrea (statement at the Annual Ministerial Meeting of the Foreign Ministers of the Least Developed Countries, 26 September 2025)
a1059.name: Osman Saleh
a1059.title: Foreign Minister of Eritrea (statement at the Annual Ministerial Meeting of the Foreign Ministers of the Least Developed Countries, 26 September 2025)
a1059.speech: "The least developed countries continue to bear the brunt of a largely unequal international system. The Sustainable Development Goals and the Doha Program of Action, are not on the right track. Global commitments to redress the historical injustices suffered by LDCs have largely remained unimplemented. This reality has been exacerbated by the overlapping global crises for which our States are not responsible." ; "It is this grim reality that makes our meeting today both urgent and timely. And I would like to take this opportunity to thank the Chair for convening this important meeting."

a1059.speaker: Osman Saleh, Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.name: Osman Saleh
a1059.title: Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.speech: "For Eritrea, the challenges we have faced and continue to face are deeply rooted in a history of colonial exploitation and a long-standing struggle to preserve our sovereignty and independence. External threats have consistently hampered our development. The illegal unilateral sanctions have strangled our economy and limited our access to finance and technology. The repeated acts of aggression against our nation and sinister policies aimed at undermining our very existence have forced us to divert limited resources away from essential development programs toward defending our sovereignty and territorial integrity." ; "Beyond these external constraints, our main obstacles remain structural. After independence, Eritrea inherited a fragile economic base, underdeveloped infrastructure, and a weak system for the provision of social services, inadequate human and institutional capacities and persistent food insecurity, further exacerbated by growing climate vulnerability."

a1059.speaker: Osman Saleh, Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.name: Osman Saleh
a1059.title: Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.speech: "In the face of all these challenges, Eritrea has chosen a path of strategic defiance and national resilience grounded on a development model predicated on the principle of self-reliance and mobilization of our greatest asset: our people." ; "We have refused to rely on food aid. Instead, we have launched nationwide campaigns through large-scale projects to conserve soil and water, lay terraces, and build small, medium and large dams. Our focus has always been on empowering our farming communities to sustain themselves and to feed the nation and to lay a conducive ground for scaling up productivity and food sovereignty." ; "We invest heavily in education and health, and we prioritize access to basic social services, prioritizing the disadvantaged peoples in the periphery and hard to reach communities... We are expanding critical infrastructure programs relying, primarily, on our national human and material resources, ensuring ownership and sustainability." ; "Today, Eritrea is a symbol of peace and stability in a region characterized by constant insecurity and instability. We have consistently contributed to efforts aimed at ensuring regional security, recognizing that there can be no development without peace and no peace without security."

a1059.speaker: Osman Saleh, Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.name: Osman Saleh
a1059.title: Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.speech: "Although Eritrea has very little debt burden, we believe that the current international system, which allows for coercive measures and perpetuates the financial structures that trap countries in debt, is fundamentally incompatible with the aspirations of the Doha Program of Action and the global agenda of sustainable development goals." ; "Therefore, our call today must not focus merely on more aid, but on securing justice, equality and structural changes needed to address the historical imbalances and inequalities that have placed Least Developed Countries in this unacceptable and vulnerable situation. We must strengthen South-South cooperation through the sharing of appropriate and affordable technologies, know-how and expertise. And, we must also resist all efforts to weaken our collective voice and speak with a united voice to claim our rightful place in the global system."

a1059.speaker: Osman Saleh, Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.name: Osman Saleh
a1059.title: Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.speech: "We must also call with one voice and in solidarity for the immediate and unconditional lifting of all illegal unilateral sanctions that are crippling the economies of the targeted least developed countries."

a1059.speaker: Osman Saleh, Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.name: Osman Saleh
a1059.title: Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.speech: "The commitments contained in the outcome of the fourth international conference on financing for development and the long-standing commitments to provide official development assistance for LDCs must be fulfilled without further delay or precondition. Such support must be direct, predictable, and in line with our national priorities." ; "Above all, the international financial institutions, the development system and all relevant UN bodies must be reformed to give the least developed countries a meaningful voice that helps in accelerating the implementation of past and future pledges and commitments addressing the special situation they found themselves in."

a1059.speaker: Osman Saleh, Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.name: Osman Saleh
a1059.title: Foreign Minister of Eritrea
a1059.speech: "In conclusion, Eritrea remains committed to the principles, priorities and deliverables of the Doha Programme of Action and the Sustainable Development Goals, and believes that achieving them requires a fundamental break with the failed models of the past, so that we can ensure the fulfilment of commitments, respect for national ownership, the unconditional removal of barriers to development and a genuine global partnership based on solidarity rather than charity." ; "Furthermore, the means of implementation and follow-up, evaluation and monitoring must be strengthened. This will allow us to deliver on promises to achieve sustainable and inclusive development that leaves no one behind." ; "As the midterm review of Doha Programme of Action approaches, we fully support the ministerial declaration we are adopting today, and we hope that this collective voice contributes to the achievement of the UN 80 theme 'Better Together', because only together can we achieve the Sustainable Development Goals and the Doha Programme of Action."

a1161.speaker: Preliminary local, regional and national studies
a1161.name: Preliminary local
a1161.title: regional and national studies
a1161.speech: Point to the near certainty of a drought this year, particularly in the southern parts of the country.

a1439.speaker: Office of the President of the United States, Donald Trump (statement)
a1439.name: Office of the President of the United States
a1439.title: Donald Trump (statement)
a1439.speech: A statement from the Office of the US President, Donald Trump, said that HIV treatment and some assistance that was under the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) may continue during the suspension of aid.

a1439.speaker: US State Department
a1439.name: US State Department
a1439.speech: said that the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) has been included in the waiver for life-saving humanitarian assistance during the 90-day suspension of foreign aid. Among the activities permitted are care for people living with HIV for the purpose of saving lives, testing and counselling, prevention and treatment of tuberculosis infection, laboratory services, and the procurement and distribution of health commodities and medicines; PEPFAR has also been permitted to provide services to prevent mother-to-child transmission.

a1439.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a1439.name: Donald Trump
a1439.title: President of the United States
a1439.speech: hours after taking office on January 20, ordered a suspension of foreign aid so that it could be reviewed to see whether it aligns with his "America First" foreign policy.

a1439.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a1439.name: Marco Rubio
a1439.title: US Secretary of State
a1439.speech: initially issued a waiver for emergency food aid and then on Tuesday for life-saving medicines, medical services, food, shelter and subsistence assistance.

a1439.speaker: Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy, US State Department (statement seen by Reuters)
a1439.name: Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy
a1439.title: US State Department (statement seen by Reuters)
a1439.speech: issued a statement clarifying that PEPFAR was included in the January 28 notice and explaining which activities are allowed: medical services and care for people living with HIV for the purpose of saving lives, including testing and counselling, prevention and treatment of infections such as tuberculosis (TB), laboratory services and the procurement and distribution of health commodities and medicines, as well as services to prevent mother-to-child transmission. "Any other activities not explicitly mentioned in this guidance may not resume without specific approval," the statement said.

a1439.speaker: Two sources with knowledge of the discussions (anonymous)
a1439.name: Two sources with knowledge of the discussions (anonymous)
a1439.speech: said on January 31 that the Trump administration is also taking steps to reduce USAID's authority and place it under the State Department, in what would be a major change in how Washington allocates US foreign aid.

a1439.speaker: US Treasury figures
a1439.name: US Treasury figures
a1439.speech: According to US Treasury data, on Monday, January 27, USAID paid out $8 million, and the previous week a total of $545 million.

a1519.speaker: N.J Ayuk, Executive Chairman of the African Energy Chamber (AEC)
a1519.name: N.J Ayuk
a1519.title: Executive Chairman of the African Energy Chamber (AEC)
a1519.speech: Called for African countries to invest at least $15 billion annually in the oil and gas sector to harness the resource potential of that industry for sustainable development, and stressed that despite the global clamour for transitioning to clean energy, African countries could not be compelled to leave the hydrocarbon resources untapped and wallow in energy poverty.

a1519.speaker: N.J Ayuk, Executive Chairman of the African Energy Chamber (AEC)
a1519.name: N.J Ayuk
a1519.title: Executive Chairman of the African Energy Chamber (AEC)
a1519.speech: Said Africa was responsible for less than four per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions and was not the cause of the climate problem ; "The wealthy nations that have used oil and gas to drive their economies and develop at the expense of poor nations like Ghana and other emerging countries are the ones that need to decarbonise; Africa needs to industrialise; and we will invest in that sector for our benefit." ; "The climate crisis is called global warming and not Africa warming; those who want to transition to green energy can do it, but Africans must be left to do it at their own pace."

a1519.speaker: N.J Ayuk, Executive Chairman of the African Energy Chamber (AEC)
a1519.name: N.J Ayuk
a1519.title: Executive Chairman of the African Energy Chamber (AEC)
a1519.speech: Said there were 600 million Africans without electricity and 900 million without clean cooking technologies - mostly women - "and that is a huge human rights issue that has to be addressed" ; He also said the developed world had no moral right to ask Ghana and other African countries to be radical about the green transition because they promised climate funds for a long time but had failed to keep that commitment ; "The money has not come, so how dare they tell Ghana to abandon her oil and gas and wait for green energy! It is not possible!" ; "The United States is saying we need to produce more oil and coal; the United Kingdom is giving out 247 licences to produce more oil; China is building coal plants together with India, and you are telling Ghana to be in the dark and say they are making a transition?"

a1519.speaker: John Abdulai Jinapor, Minister of Energy and Green Transition of Ghana (speech delivered on his behalf by Deputy Minister of Energy Richard Gyan-Mensah)
a1519.name: John Abdulai Jinapor
a1519.title: Minister of Energy and Green Transition of Ghana (speech delivered on his behalf by Deputy Minister of Energy Richard Gyan-Mensah)
a1519.speech: Said that with 125 billion barrels of oil, 600 trillion cubic feet of gas, the huge renewable energy potential and the huge amount of mineral deposits, including green minerals, it was worrying that Africa was still grappling with energy poverty, and said the situation existed because of funding, technology, infrastructure and market constraints ; "It is, therefore, imperative to design and implement realistic and pragmatic approaches to attract the needed capital to develop and harness the full potential of our energy resources."

a1519.speaker: John Abdulai Jinapor, Minister of Energy and Green Transition of Ghana
a1519.name: John Abdulai Jinapor
a1519.title: Minister of Energy and Green Transition of Ghana
a1519.speech: Said that as part of Ghana's ultimate goal to ensure energy security, the country was pursuing policy reforms to attract investments in renewables such as solar and wind and renewable energy forms such as oil and gas; he said the government was also prioritising storage and transportation infrastructure, as well as innovation to maximise the benefits of hydrocarbon resources and other energy resources.

a1564.speaker: Opposition lawmakers attending the CMC convention
a1564.name: Opposition lawmakers attending the CMC convention
a1564.speech: Welcomed the establishment of a new political party to counter the ruling establishment, which they say has failed the Liberian people.

a1564.speaker: Musa Hassan Bility, Nimba County District #7 Representative and CMC Political Leader
a1564.name: Musa Hassan Bility
a1564.title: Nimba County District #7 Representative and CMC Political Leader
a1564.speech: Said that for the last 30 years he walked the path of politics, fighting to make things right, pushing for a better Liberia, trying to convince those in power to lead with vision and responsibility. “I have given my time, my energy, my ideas, and my heart to this country. But I have come to realize that true change cannot come from the top unless the people own it, demand it, and drive it forward themselves. That is why we are here today.” ; “We are here to chart a new course—one where Liberians are not just spectators but participants in building their nation. One where our economy is not controlled by a few, but by the many. One where our women, our children, our farmers, our entrepreneurs, our workers, and our youth have a place and a purpose. This is your movement. This is the Citizen Movement for Change (CMC). This is the movement that will transform Liberia from a country of survival to a country of prosperity.”

a1564.speaker: Yekeh Korlubah, Montserrado County District #10 Representative
a1564.name: Yekeh Korlubah
a1564.title: Montserrado County District #10 Representative
a1564.speech: Assured the people of Nimba County that he will be in the forefront of the campaign for the Nimba County senator, and that he will work with the CMC to ensure an opposition victory because the ruling establishment has failed the Liberian people; therefore, any candidate supported by the government in these by-elections will be a disservice to the people of Nimba County and the Liberian people. “I want to challenge some of you lawmakers. Some people say they want to be senators, but they are breaking all the laws. The law you made, you are breaking it, but you want to go up... You cannot be a gangster, then you want to run Nimba County. You cannot be a lawmaker that is breaking the law that we made ourselves, then you want to be senator of Nimba County. You are wasting your time. We will be here. And the opposition will take the day... Nobody campaigned for this government equally to me, but what we campaigned for is not happening and will never happen.”

a1564.speaker: Yekeh Korlubah, Montserrado County District #10 Representative
a1564.name: Yekeh Korlubah
a1564.title: Montserrado County District #10 Representative
a1564.speech: Said Liberia will only progress if Liberians come together and understand that they themselves are their own problem. “Liberia will be better when we all come together, because our problem in this country is about ourselves; it's not about a leader... Are we going to live like this: where when your interest is there then everything is ok?... I am not criticizing because I want to criticize. I am criticizing because when we said yesterday, former President Weah was riding a private jet, but the Joseph Boakai I brought to power is riding a private jet from here to go to Lofa County... I have no regret voting against former President Weah. But the people I brought to power will regret why I had to vote for them and campaign for them.” ; “This country is a better place and will be a better place because there is money in this country we can live on; we don't need money from outside. But we don't want to empower people here. We sit down as lawmakers, we have become lawbreakers, we have become criminals. We put all the money in the budget and leave you the people out.”

a1564.speaker: Josiah Marvin Cole, Representative of District #3, Bong County
a1564.name: Josiah Marvin Cole
a1564.title: Representative of District #3, Bong County
a1564.speech: Said, as a member of the opposition bloc, the Coalition for Democratic Change (CDC), he will ensure Representative Samuel Kogar does not become the next senator for Nimba County: “Two reasons why Samuel Kogar should not be elected as senator of Nimba County. He is going to create a byelection that will be a financial burden to the already drowned political institution or conversation they are having with the Unity Party, which has failed this country and Kogar is associating with them. So, to contest as a senator for Nimba, if you win that election, you are going to create a by-election that will be very dangerous.” ; “With Senator Nya Twayen in Nimba County, you can see his performance... So, if Representative Kogar comes and says he wants to be senator, just one major reason he cannot be senator is that Kogar could not manage his home. The woman had to take him to court... The court has ruled against him to retroactively pay US$1,000 of his earnings to this woman. So, Kogar, there is no reason that you have a job already which you messed up. You cannot represent the people of Nimba and you want to be a senator.”

a1564.speaker: Josiah Marvin Cole, Representative of District #3, Bong County
a1564.name: Josiah Marvin Cole
a1564.title: Representative of District #3, Bong County
a1564.speech: On his attendance at the CMC convention: “We are all in Nimba County, Saclepea. We came to support our colleague Musa Hassan Bility... The whole country and other political leaders are concerned about why I am wearing the party T-shirt of the CMC. I have not officially joined the CMC. We have come as members of the Rule of Law Caucus to support Musa Bility because he is our chairman... If the need arises to join, we are going to make a full disclosure of our intent to join the CMC.” ; “In the county, across the country, we have a commanding lead in the Bong County politics. Anybody who won with around 20,000 votes, you are a determining factor in any election in the Republic of Liberia. But I can tell you, I support the opposition, and we will be supporting the opposition candidate in Nimba County that will be a winnable candidate.” He also encouraged Musa Hassan Bility and all the members of the CMC to continue.

a1616.speaker: US Department of Homeland Security (DHS)
a1616.name: US Department of Homeland Security (DHS)
a1616.speech: On Thursday, attributed the revocation of Harvard's Student and Exchange Visitor Programme certification to the university's refusal to comply with its requests for the behavioural records of student visa holders.

a1616.speaker: Kristi Noem, US Homeland Security Secretary
a1616.name: Kristi Noem
a1616.title: US Homeland Security Secretary
a1616.speech: In a post on X, accused the school of fostering an unsafe campus environment, hostility to Jewish students, support for Hamas, and what she described as racist DEI initiatives: "Let this serve as a warning to all universities and academic institutions across the country. This administration is holding Harvard accountable for fostering violence, antisemitism, and coordinating with the Chinese Communist Party on its campus" ; "It is a privilege, not a right, for universities to enrol foreign students and benefit from their higher tuition payments to help pad their multibillion-dollar endowments. Harvard had plenty of opportunities to do the right thing. It refused." ; "They have lost their Student and Exchange Visitor Program certification as a result of their failure to adhere to the law."

a1616.speaker: Kristi Noem, US Homeland Security Secretary (letter to Harvard University)
a1616.name: Kristi Noem
a1616.title: US Homeland Security Secretary (letter to Harvard University)
a1616.speech: Described this as a consequence of Harvard's refusal to comply with "simple reporting requirements": "As a result of your brazen refusal to comply with multiple requests to provide the Department of Homeland Security pertinent information while perpetuating an unsafe campus environment that is hostile to Jewish students, promotes pro-Hamas rhetoric, and employs racist 'diversity, equity, and inclusion' policies, you have lost this privilege." She, however, offered the institution 72 hours to provide the information requested for an opportunity to regain its visa programme for the next school year.

a1616.speaker: The Trump administration
a1616.name: The Trump administration
a1616.speech: Said Harvard may no longer enrol foreign students in the 2025-2026 school year, and stated that existing foreign students must transfer or lose their legal status to reside in the US before the next academic year begins.

a1616.speaker: Harvard University (statement)
a1616.name: Harvard University (statement)
a1616.speech: Denounced the allegations made against it and described the directive as retaliatory action that threatens its community, reaffirming its commitment to campus safety, academic freedom, and support for all students: "We are fully committed to maintaining Harvard's ability to host our international students and scholars, who hail from more than 140 countries and enrich the University - and this nation - immeasurably." ; "We are working quickly to provide guidance and support to members of our community. This retaliatory action threatens serious harm to the Harvard community and our country, and undermines Harvard's academic and research mission."

a1616.speaker: Harvard University's One World programme
a1616.name: Harvard University's One World programme
a1616.speech: According to it, the Ivy League institution has so far enrolled about 6,793 international students, representing about 27.2 per cent of its total student body.

a1616.speaker: US Department of Education
a1616.name: US Department of Education
a1616.speech: In March, launched an investigation into the university and 51 other schools, accusing them of racial preference and stereotypes in education programmes.

a1616.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES (earlier report)
a1616.name: PREMIUM TIMES (earlier report)
a1616.speech: Reported that about 600 international students in over 90 colleges and universities have had their visas revoked or their legal status terminated in the last months.

a1616.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a1616.name: Marco Rubio
a1616.title: US Secretary of State
a1616.speech: Said the State Department had likely revoked thousands of student visas across the country and was open to revoking more: "We're going to continue to revoke the visas of people who are here as guests and are disrupting our higher education facilities. A visa is a privilege, not a right," he said to Congress on Tuesday.

a1686.speaker: General Auditing Commission (GAC) of Liberia (statement)
a1686.name: General Auditing Commission (GAC) of Liberia (statement)
a1686.speech: "We would like to express our thanks and appreciation to the Honorable Comptroller General of the United States and Head of the U.S. Government Accountability Office, Mr. Gene L. Dodaro, and his team for the recognition, collaboration and invaluable opportunity to enhance the capacity of our staff at the GAC. Special thanks also go to the U.S. State Department and the U.S. Embassy in Liberia for the respective roles they played in validating the impact of our work, leading towards the signing of this MoU," a statement from the GAC released on Friday said.

a1723.speaker: Kristèle Younes, Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Guinea
a1723.name: Kristèle Younes
a1723.title: Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Guinea
a1723.speech: Invited the international institutions and embassies to act in synergy to face Guinea's emergencies: "The moment is critical. The 2030 horizon is approaching fast, and Guinea, like many other countries, faces a simple but urgent reality: we need bold action and appropriate financing to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The question of financing is not only about how many resources we can mobilise, but it is also and above all about how these resources can be used optimally to respond to the country's priorities. I hope that this dialogue will mark a crucial step in our collective commitment to change the current trajectory of the SDGs and to unlock the full potential of financing for the benefit of the Guinean people, particularly the most vulnerable. Under the impetus of the Ministry of Planning and International Cooperation, we [international institutions] have the opportunity to be the architects of this transformation, to achieve Agenda 2030, which requires considerable investment and an innovative approach to financing."

a1723.speaker: Ismaël Nabé, Guinean Minister of Planning and International Cooperation
a1723.name: Ismaël Nabé
a1723.title: Guinean Minister of Planning and International Cooperation
a1723.speech: Stated that Guinea faces a multi-sector crisis: "(...) We are facing financial crises brought on by multiple crises which hinder the full achievement of the SDGs, particularly in the area of regional inequalities, access to basic services and resilience in the face of climate shocks."

a1723.speaker: Ismaël Nabé, Guinean Minister of Planning and International Cooperation
a1723.name: Ismaël Nabé
a1723.title: Guinean Minister of Planning and International Cooperation
a1723.speech: Made a plea to Guinea's partner institutions setting out three priority areas: "To meet these challenges, I wanted to insist on three priority areas within this framework. First, mobilise innovative and diversified resources. Traditional financing, although important, is no longer enough. Guinea advocates an approach that combines public-private partnerships to attract private capital into infrastructure and energy projects, but also innovative financing mechanisms such as green bonds and results-based financing adapted to specific projects. Second, strengthen international solidarity and South-South cooperation. In this regard, Guinea calls for increased support from bilateral and multilateral partnerships, the intensification of triangular and circular South-South cooperation, which constitutes a strategic lever for adapted and sustainable solutions. Third, guarantee effectiveness and transparency in the use of resources, and rigorous and transparent management of essential resources in order to inspire partners' confidence and maximise financing when Guinea needs it." ; "Guinea, for its part, undertakes to strengthen institutional capacities, particularly through high-performing monitoring and evaluation systems. We also undertake to align investments with national priorities, while ensuring effective coordination with partners."

a1723.speaker: Mourana Soumah, Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a1723.name: Mourana Soumah
a1723.title: Guinean Minister of Economy and Finance
a1723.speech: Spoke of the importance of financing in a country's development: "(...) There is no development without financing. So, as there is no development without financing, there must be synergy of action since we will indeed reach the 2030 target. This financing must be mobilised internationally, but national efforts must also cover a good part of the financing needs. In addition to international financing, we must mobilise sufficient domestic resources and therefore have a substantial tax take that allows us fiscal space to finance very important development items in our budget. Where we have immense needs to build, for example, schools, health centres, regional hospitals."

a1947.speaker: Residents (of Zamfara)
a1947.name: Residents (of Zamfara)
a1947.speech: Said the terrorists used a bus for the operation, instead of their usual motorcycles, so as to beat security and local intelligence.

a1947.speaker: Haruna Malam, a resident
a1947.name: Haruna Malam
a1947.title: a resident
a1947.speech: Told reporters that the gang moved the passengers from their vehicles at gunpoint into a bus parked a few meters from the main road.

a1947.speaker: Usman Dantsoho, a tree cutter from Gadarmanya village of Anka LGA who escaped the abduction
a1947.name: Usman Dantsoho
a1947.title: a tree cutter from Gadarmanya village of Anka LGA who escaped the abduction
a1947.speech: Said he saw the terrorists’ bus riding with the victims into the forest. “I was in the bush with my cart to cut trees and fetch my dried firewood that I kept, only to hear four rounds gunshot from the Anka-Bukuyum road. I quickly ran away from my location and climbed up a tree. I saw the armed gang attack a moving vehicle and abducted the people in it. I returned home only to be told that the vice chairman of Bukuyum LGA was among those kidnapped.”

a1947.speaker: Abubakar Sadiq, police spokesperson in Zamfara
a1947.name: Abubakar Sadiq
a1947.title: police spokesperson in Zamfara
a1947.speech: Could not be reached on phone to comment on the development.

a2116.speaker: Ben M'bwana, Director of Administration at the Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare (Malawi)
a2116.name: Ben M'bwana
a2116.title: Director of Administration at the Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare (Malawi)
a2116.speech: Emphasized the significance of bicycles beyond transportation: "Bicycles are not just a means of transport; they are a transformative tool for development and empowerment."

a2116.speaker: Matola
a2116.name: Matola
a2116.speech: "we would have spent billions of Kwacha if this were to be done by expatriates elsewhere."

a2184.speaker: Ahunna Eziakonwa, Director of the Regional Bureau for Africa at the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), speaking at the 2024 African Economic Conference in Gaborone, Botswana (according to a statement released by ECA)
a2184.name: Ahunna Eziakonwa
a2184.title: Director of the Regional Bureau for Africa at the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), speaking at the 2024 African Economic Conference in Gaborone, Botswana (according to a statement released by ECA)
a2184.speech: said Africa is experiencing numerous successes, yet these achievements go unnoticed as the positive stories of the continent's progress are not being told, and that Africa has suffered from being viewed through a negative lens, with this lack of a positive narrative perpetuating negative stereotypes: "There is always this sense that Africa is this place where donors have to dump their charitable acts. Because we are going to Africa with aid we have people there with no strength and brains." ; she said this is one of the burdens of the continent and that it is very important to change that narrative, which will have to come from Africans telling their story of the dynamism and diversity of the continent ; she emphasised that Africa has endured a legacy of stereotyping and being synonymous with failure, which needs to change: "Africa should present itself as a continent that thrives and upholds the spirit of common humanity."

a2184.speaker: Ahunna Eziakonwa, Director of the Regional Bureau for Africa at UNDP
a2184.name: Ahunna Eziakonwa
a2184.title: Director of the Regional Bureau for Africa at UNDP
a2184.speech: called on Africans to share the continent's achievements and urged leaders to avoid false celebrations of excellence: "We need more African writers telling the story of Africa and we should stop this self-adulation, particularly at the level of leaders, when we celebrate excellence when there is none. It is about leadership and governance."

a2184.speaker: Ahunna Eziakonwa, Director of the Regional Bureau for Africa at UNDP
a2184.name: Ahunna Eziakonwa
a2184.title: Director of the Regional Bureau for Africa at UNDP
a2184.speech: believes that a significant part of reshaping Africa's narrative involves empowering young people; she notes that in many African cultures the youth are expected to be seen and not heard, but highlighted Botswana's recent cabinet appointments, which included more members under 50, as an example of progress: "We are seeing more young people being recognised but the investment in making young people succeed in whatever they do has not been done."

a2184.speaker: Ahunna Eziakonwa, Director of the Regional Bureau for Africa at UNDP
a2184.name: Ahunna Eziakonwa
a2184.title: Director of the Regional Bureau for Africa at UNDP
a2184.speech: Regarding foreign aid, cautioned that it has often done more harm than good to Africa's psyche and institutions, due to how it has been structured; she said aid comes at a cost and consumes much of Africa's energy and attention while offering diminishing returns: "We have to be more innovative and we need to correct this sense that Africa is trapped in aid."

a2189.speaker: Barry Rassin, Rotary International President
a2189.name: Barry Rassin
a2189.title: Rotary International President
a2189.speech: Confirmed Rotary's commitment to supporting Ethiopia's polio eradication efforts, both at the national level and through Rotarians' volunteer activities aimed at educating communities about polio and ensuring every child is immunized.

a2189.speaker: Barry Rassin, Rotary International President
a2189.name: Barry Rassin
a2189.title: Rotary International President
a2189.speech: Commended the work done so far to render the country polio free: "You have done wonderful work, but you still need to remain vigilant" ; "Now the hard work starts; we need to reach out to every child along every border or else this disease can blow up in no time. This is critical and Rotary is committed through the end."

a2189.speaker: Barry Rassin, Rotary International President
a2189.name: Barry Rassin
a2189.title: Rotary International President
a2189.speech: Said the strong partnership between the Government and Rotary played a key role in helping the organization carry out successful activities in Ethiopia; pledged to continue cooperating with the Ethiopian government ; "It is because of this high level engagement and leadership that Ethiopia has succeeded in maintaining its polio-free status, even as other areas of the Horn of Africa are affected by a polio outbreak."

a2189.speaker: Barry Rassin, Rotary International President
a2189.name: Barry Rassin
a2189.title: Rotary International President
a2189.speech: Said the Regional Service Award presented to Rotarian Mohammed Idris is a high level recognition from the Rotary Foundation Trustees' Chair, Paul A Netzel.

a2189.speaker: Dr. Lia Tadesse, State Minister of Health of Ethiopia
a2189.name: Dr. Lia Tadesse
a2189.title: State Minister of Health of Ethiopia
a2189.speech: Expressed her appreciation for Rotary's support in eradicating polio from the country; said that it has been five years since polio transmission was interrupted in Ethiopia and that her ministry would work to ensure that it doesn't return in the horn of Africa; said that the Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH) will ensure routine polio immunizations are conducted regularly, especially in critical areas along the borders of the country.

a2189.speaker: Federal Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (polio transition plan)
a2189.name: Federal Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (polio transition plan)
a2189.speech: According to the FMoH, the objectives outlined in Ethiopia's polio transition plan are to maintain its polio free status and to ensure that in a post eradication era, Ethiopia can continue to address its most pressing public health and humanitarian needs by applying the lessons learned through its polio eradication efforts; there is a budget deficit of around 12 million USD which the FMoH is working on raising.

a2189.speaker: Olayinka Hakeem Babalola, Rotary International Director
a2189.name: Olayinka Hakeem Babalola
a2189.title: Rotary International Director
a2189.speech: Noted that intensive surveillance is critical to ensure potential cases are detected quickly in all the countries of the region; stressed that this work is an important part of guaranteeing that Africa can achieve its polio free status, assuring that Rotary will be working together with all stakeholders until polio is completely eliminated from the world.

a2189.speaker: Sahle-Work Zewde, President of Ethiopia
a2189.name: Sahle-Work Zewde
a2189.title: President of Ethiopia
a2189.speech: Said that the government will provide all the necessary support for the organization's activities in Ethiopia; further said a new civil society law was recently ratified by Parliament in order to create favorable conditions for non-governmental organizations.

a2189.speaker: Samson Tesfaye, Rotary International Representative to the African Union and United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
a2189.name: Samson Tesfaye
a2189.title: Rotary International Representative to the African Union and United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
a2189.speech: Said that the discussion revolved around the partnership between Rotary International and the African Union Commission, and that the "African Union's vision of Agenda 2063 and Rotary's six areas of focus have shared values that can pave way for an area of collaboration between the two organizations for the betterment of the African population."

a2189.speaker: Azeb Asrat, Rotary Country Chair
a2189.name: Azeb Asrat
a2189.title: Rotary Country Chair
a2189.speech: "What an honor and privilege to have the visit of RI President and senior Rotary officials to Ethiopia." Such a visit will inspire local Rotarians and encourage voluntarism. "Rotary stands to change lives."

a2189.speaker: Ezra Teshome, Past District Governor
a2189.name: Ezra Teshome
a2189.title: Past District Governor
a2189.speech: "Rtn. Mohamed has worked tirelessly, since the start of the GPEI (global polio eradication initiative) first with WHO and then with Rotary through the National Polio Plus Committee, liaising with MoH, partners and allies."

a2196.speaker: Governs Kwame Agbodza, Minister for Roads and Highways of Ghana
a2196.name: Governs Kwame Agbodza
a2196.title: Minister for Roads and Highways of Ghana
a2196.speech: Says government has cleared all arrears on the Ofankor–Nsawam highway project, paying more than US$77 million to settle debts owed to the contractor; stated that the outstanding certificates that had led to delays have now been fully paid ; "In excess of US$77 million. So as of today, we don't owe the contractor a penny; every certificate raised, which was outstanding before we came to power, based upon which they abandoned the site, we have paid fully" ; expressed confidence that with the financial bottleneck cleared, work on the critical highway should progress without further interruption.

a2196.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2196.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2196.title: President of Ghana
a2196.speech: Urged the contractor to speed up construction, warning that excuses for delay would not be entertained: "Expedite construction and deliver the project within the stipulated timeline."

a2196.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2196.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2196.title: President of Ghana
a2196.speech: Revealed that the project has now been captured under the government's Big Push programme; said GHC14 billion has already been allocated to the initiative this year, with an additional GHC30 billion expected in 2026: "There will be sufficient resources to keep the contractors going."

a2639.speaker: Somali officials
a2639.name: Somali officials
a2639.speech: Say the step of formally joining the International Atomic Energy Agency will boost the country’s health care, food security, and energy development.

a2639.speaker: Ambassador Khadra Ahmed Dualeh, Somalia's envoy to Austria and Switzerland and first permanent envoy to the IAEA
a2639.name: Ambassador Khadra Ahmed Dualeh
a2639.title: Somalia's envoy to Austria and Switzerland and first permanent envoy to the IAEA
a2639.speech: Described IAEA membership as a strategic milestone. “Somalia will gain technical support and advice on the peaceful use of nuclear energy, particularly in electricity generation. This could reduce reliance on fuel imports while boosting economic development,” she told the BBC.

a2639.speaker: Office of Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre
a2639.name: Office of Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre
a2639.speech: Described the step as “a historic moment,” framing it as part of Somalia’s wider attempt to rebuild trust abroad while investing in sustainable development.

a2639.speaker: Daud Aweis, Information Minister
a2639.name: Daud Aweis
a2639.title: Information Minister
a2639.speech: Telling Anadolu that the government hoped to work closely with the international community to channel nuclear technology into tangible gains “for the benefit of our nation,” while stressing the need for rigorous safety and security standards.

a2639.speaker: Government of Somalia (official statement)
a2639.name: Government of Somalia (official statement)
a2639.speech: In its official statement, the government was keen to emphasize continuity with international norms. It pledged adherence to nonproliferation rules and promised cooperation with fellow IAEA members on peaceful applications such as power generation, radiation protection and nuclear safety.

a2639.speaker: Almond Energy (Somali consultancy firm, own estimates)
a2639.name: Almond Energy (Somali consultancy firm
a2639.title: own estimates)
a2639.speech: By the firm’s own estimates, Somalia’s uranium deposits may lie under as much as 40 percent of Somali territory.

a2639.speaker: Experts/geologists (1970s-1980s surveys, cited)
a2639.name: Experts/geologists (1970s-1980s surveys
a2639.title: cited)
a2639.speech: Experts estimated there were a few thousand tons of uranium at Wabo and Mirig, with more possible in nearby areas such as Dusa Mareb and El Bur. An international survey in the 1980s suggested the country could hold much larger reserves, perhaps as much as 150,000 tons, mostly in the sandy, desert-like plains of Mudugh and Karkar.

a2639.speaker: 1985 report on Somalia's uranium findings (cited)
a2639.name: 1985 report on Somalia's uranium findings (cited)
a2639.speech: Painted a stark picture of Somalia’s capacity at the time: the country’s Geological Survey was short of equipment, its laboratories were underused, and its files and data were poorly managed. Without international support, the report warned, Somalia would struggle to develop its uranium resources.

a2841.speaker: United Nations
a2841.name: United Nations
a2841.speech: said it requires $1.42 billion to increase humanitarian actions in Somalia, where 5.98 million people will need humanitarian assistance in 2025.

a2841.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2841.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2841.speech: Launching its 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) for Somalia on Sunday, said 4.6 million people will be targeted for assistance focusing on lifesaving and life-sustaining assistance for people with the most severe needs ; noting that drought and conflict could be among key risks in 2025, it added drier conditions will increase competition over resources, and heighten risks for disease outbreaks.

a2841.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2841.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2841.speech: said conflict accounted for 53% of a total of 455,000 newly displaced people in the horn of Africa country, while climate shocks accounted for the vast majority of displacements in 2022 and 2023.

a2841.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2841.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2841.speech: said in 2024, the humanitarian situation in Somalia saw slight improvements as compared to previous years, marked by a devastating drought in 2020-23 and severe flooding late last year.

a2849.speaker: Pensions and Insurance Authority (PIA)
a2849.name: Pensions and Insurance Authority (PIA)
a2849.speech: Says there is need to intensify awareness and increase understanding of insurance services to raise the uptake in the country.

a2849.speaker: Patrick Lumumba, Pan-Africanist
a2849.name: Patrick Lumumba
a2849.title: Pan-Africanist
a2849.speech: Has advised former President Edgar Lungu to retire and leave the stage honourably following the Constitutional Court judgment that he is ineligible.

a2849.speaker: Evangelical Fellowship of Zambia (EFZ)
a2849.name: Evangelical Fellowship of Zambia (EFZ)
a2849.speech: Says the nation should not remain static but move on now that the eligibility case has been decided.

a2849.speaker: Over a dozen Patriotic Front (PF) Members of Parliament
a2849.name: Over a dozen Patriotic Front (PF) Members of Parliament
a2849.speech: Have asked former President Edgar Lungu to finally assume the role of statesman.

a2857.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi and outgoing SADC chairperson
a2857.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a2857.title: President of Malawi and outgoing SADC chairperson
a2857.speech: Told the media in Malawi that he leaves the leadership role a happy man.

a2857.speaker: Felix Tshisekedi, President of the DRC
a2857.name: Felix Tshisekedi
a2857.title: President of the DRC
a2857.speech: Accuses Rwanda of working with the rebels in the eastern part of the DRC.

a2857.speaker: Ringisai Chikohomero, research consultant with the Institute of Security Studies in Pretoria
a2857.name: Ringisai Chikohomero
a2857.title: research consultant with the Institute of Security Studies in Pretoria
a2857.speech: Hopes Eswatini would be discussed at the summit: “The regional body needs a bold and clear position on the next steps - such as assigning a high-level envoy to the kingdom. For the pro-democracy movement, there’s a sense that the king is being handled with kid gloves while Eswatini sinks into turmoil.”

a2857.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa, Macky Sall, President of Senegal, and Emmanuel Macron, President of France (letter published in the international media)
a2857.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a2857.title: President of South Africa, Macky Sall, President of Senegal, and Emmanuel Macron, President of France (letter published in the international media)
a2857.speech: “It is difficult to build a vaccine production unit, but it is even more difficult to ensure its sustainability” ; called for investment in pandemic preparedness.

a2857.speaker: Presidency | South Africa (@PresidencyZA), social media post, August 16, 2022
a2857.name: Presidency | South Africa (@PresidencyZA)
a2857.title: social media post, August 16, 2022
a2857.speech: “His Excellency President @CyrilRamaphosa is this morning undertaking a Working Visit to Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo where he will be participating in the 42nd Ordinary Summit of the Southern African Development Community Heads of State & Government. #SADCSummit”

a2857.speaker: Nancy Tembo, Malawi’s health minister and outgoing chairperson of the SADC council of ministers
a2857.name: Nancy Tembo
a2857.title: Malawi’s health minister and outgoing chairperson of the SADC council of ministers
a2857.speech: Said on Monday that SADC should work on “bolstering productive capacities in the face of the Covid-19 pandemic for inclusive sustainable economic and industrial transformation”.

a2857.speaker: South African Presidency (statement)
a2857.name: South African Presidency (statement)
a2857.speech: Said part of the summit would dwell on climate change matters such as setting up a regional response hub, noting that SADC leaders are meeting after the devastating Cyclone Gombe and tropical storm Batsirai, which affected parts of Madagascar, Mozambique, Malawi and Zimbabwe, leading to the displacement of hundreds of thousands of people.

a3045.speaker: Hussein Ali Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a3045.name: Hussein Ali Mwinyi
a3045.title: President of Zanzibar
a3045.speech: launched the Zanzibar Energy Policy 2025 and the Zanzibar Power Master Plan 2025-2050, pledging reliable, affordable and sustainable energy while warning against rising acts of sabotage targeting electricity infrastructure ; condemned the theft of eight electricity transformers reported within a month, describing it as a direct attack on national development: "These are people who know what they're doing. I want everyone involved to be punished."

a3045.speaker: Hussein Ali Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a3045.name: Hussein Ali Mwinyi
a3045.title: President of Zanzibar
a3045.speech: said the new policy marks "a turning point" in efforts to secure energy as the backbone of Zanzibar's social and economic transformation ; stressed that without reliable power, the isles cannot achieve the 2050 Development Vision, implement the ruling CCM manifesto (2025-2030), or grow a competitive blue economy ; said the new framework aims to expand access in rural areas while driving investment in renewables such as solar, wind, biofuels and gas ; "Our ambition is to increase access to modern energy, improve efficiency, attract private investment and build resilience against climate change" ; "This is the start of a new journey towards safe, clean, affordable and sustainable energy for current and future generations."

a3045.speaker: Hassan Shaibu Kaduara, Minister for Water, Energy and Minerals, and Joseph Kilangi, Permanent Secretary
a3045.name: Hassan Shaibu Kaduara
a3045.title: Minister for Water, Energy and Minerals, and Joseph Kilangi, Permanent Secretary

a3045.speaker: Joseph Kilangi, Permanent Secretary, Ministry for Water, Energy and Minerals
a3045.name: Joseph Kilangi
a3045.title: Permanent Secretary, Ministry for Water, Energy and Minerals
a3045.speech: said for the first time, Zanzibar's energy policy allows private-sector participation in power generation and distribution, including net metering, where households and businesses can feed surplus renewable power into the grid ; also cited upcoming initiatives such as an Energy Efficiency Strategy, a national renewable energy framework and an Energy Act to strengthen governance, reduce technical and commercial losses and promote modern energy use.

a3045.speaker: Rhonda Jordan Antoine, Senior Energy Specialist at the World Bank (representing development partners)
a3045.name: Rhonda Jordan Antoine
a3045.title: Senior Energy Specialist at the World Bank (representing development partners)
a3045.speech: praised the policy, saying it is a "blueprint for transformation" that addresses Zanzibar's vulnerabilities while supporting climate-resilient growth. "The World Bank is a steadfast partner to the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar" ; "Our portfolio, approaching 400 million US dollars across sectors, reflects our commitment. The Zanzibar Energy Policy 2025 is more than a document; it lays out a credible pathway to universal access and robust economic growth" ; highlighted the Bank's 142 million US dollars Zanzibar Energy Sector Transformation and Access Project (ZESTA), which is already financing a 132kV transmission backbone, new substations at Makunduchi and Matemwe and an 18MW solar plant at Makunduchi.

a3090.speaker: Head of the Tete Provincial branch of the National Migration Service of Mozambique (SENAMI)
a3090.name: Head of the Tete Provincial branch of the National Migration Service of Mozambique (SENAMI)
a3090.speech: Told the International Organization for Migration (IOM) that the men, who were carrying no documents, have told SENAMI they are Ethiopians traveling to South Africa; according to the official, the survivors are deeply traumatized and the driver of the vehicle is in custody.

a3090.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a3090.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a3090.speech: According to the IOM, every year more than 200,000 young Ethiopians cross the country's border in search of better opportunities and are exposed to a wide range of risks.

a3090.speaker: IOM flow monitoring survey report on movement of Ethiopian migrants (released 18 March 2020)
a3090.name: IOM flow monitoring survey report on movement of Ethiopian migrants (released 18 March 2020)
a3090.speech: As the report stated, the intended final destinations of migrants are further investigated for 3 specific reasons, namely travelling for job opportunities, ease of access to asylum procedures and ease of access to humanitarian assistance; key findings show that most of the migrants surveyed, who were 69 percent male and 21 percent female, were unemployed, the primary country of departure amongst respondents was Ethiopia, followed by Sudan and Djibouti, and the primary intended final destinations included the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Sudan and Ethiopia.

a3090.speaker: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UNDESA)
a3090.name: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UNDESA)
a3090.speech: According to UNDESA, in 2019 South Africa was home to about 4.2 million migrants, and 290,000 asylum seekers and refugees, with Zimbabwe, Somalia, Malawi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Ethiopia the main source countries.

a3114.speaker: Rep. Nicole Malliotakis, New York Republican
a3114.name: Rep. Nicole Malliotakis
a3114.title: New York Republican
a3114.speech: “Things are happening so fast and furiously. We need to take a step back and make sure that we’re doing things in a way that we are rooting out the waste, the fraud and the abuse and the mismanagement, making programs efficient but not resulting in unintended consequences.”

a3114.speaker: CNN/SSRS poll (last week)
a3114.name: CNN/SSRS poll (last week)
a3114.speech: 51% said Trump had gone too far in cutting federal programs and 53% thought it was bad that Musk is so prominent.

a3114.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3114.name: Donald Trump
a3114.title: US President
a3114.speech: “I thought it was great,” the president said Monday of his friend’s demand for federal workers to reply to an email justifying their productivity last week. ; “Well, it’s somewhat voluntary, but it’s also, if you don’t answer, I guess you get fired. What it really is, what it is, is – do people exist?”

a3114.speaker: Karoline Leavitt, White House Press Secretary
a3114.name: Karoline Leavitt
a3114.title: White House Press Secretary
a3114.speech: “The president and Elon and his entire Cabinet are working as one unified team.”

a3114.speaker: Elon Musk
a3114.name: Elon Musk
